system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: a prompt is carefully crafted for each specific defect type, tailored to repair instances of that defect category based on feedback from the static analyzer report. For each target defect type, specific additional instructions are appended to the prompt as context information.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: skills with the highest semantic similarity to steps in the natural language instructions are appended as additional context. To mitigate FMs’ known limitation of getting distracted by irrelevant context [61], after preliminary evaluations, we chose to use the third mode.
env_context_strategy.note: Other modes: all skills, or exact-match query.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: Pumbaaalso iteratively prompts the FM to repair the input workflow’s defect incidences.
context_compaction.note: No compaction mechanism described; each repair prompt is constructed per defect type.

observation_format.evidence_quote: incorporatingTimon’s report of detected defects as direct feedback for an accurate and effective repair

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: the FM in this component is prompted to generate the corresponding workflow as a valid JSON object that adheres to theWorkflowDSLgrammar
tool_call_format.note: The model emits a DSL/JSON program, not tool calls; closest value is json_in_text.

tool_count.evidence_quote: the FM in this component is prompted to generate the corresponding workflow as a valid JSON object that adheres to theWorkflowDSLgrammar
tool_count.note: No tool schemas are exposed to the model; skills are listed as prompt context, not callable tools.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: repairing a defective DSL can also be considered as re-synthesizing the program such that it correctly adheres to the structure of the specified grammar

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: For each skill, we provide the skill name, accepted input fields with their types, expected output format, and a natural-language description of the skill.
tool_schema_source.note: Skill descriptions come from a skills database.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: the Model Context Protocol [47] enables LLM-based clients to discover and execute tools at runtime via a unified interface
protocol_standardization.note: MCP only cited as related work; the pipeline uses its own skills database.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: after each repair attempt byPumbaa, the target workflow is re-examined by the static analyzer to verify whether all original defect incidences are resolved
loop_primitives.note: Pipeline: requirements refinement -> synthesis -> Timon detection -> Pumbaa repair loop.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: generate a list of step-by-step natural language instructions corresponding to their intent
planning_granularity.note: The step-by-step NL instructions and the DSL workflow itself are stored plan artifacts.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: To synthesize DSL workflows, two main components interact with each other: the Converter Agent B.1 and the Skill Chooser B.2 .
multi_agent_topology.note: AlignMind multi-agent refiner, then Converter Agent, then Timon/Pumbaa: fixed hand-off.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: it pauses the detection process and sends the invalid workflow toPumbaa. IfPumbaais able to correct the input such that it can be successfully parsed as a JSON object and instantiated as a valid DSL program, the corrected DSL program is sent back toTimon

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: after showing a detailed compilation of remaining defect types and their locations in the input FM-generated DSL workflows, the system should defer to end users and their expertise for repairing them
human_in_loop.note: Proposed fallback; also users converse with AlignMind during requirements refinement.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: a control flow graph (CFG) [ 3] is constructed B.1 by parsing the DSL representation of the workflow. Afterwards, from the con-structed CFGTimonbuildsuse-defanddef-use chains
short_term_state.note: The workflow object plus its intermediate representation and defect report are the working state.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: Timoncompares each task-corresponding action used within the workflow against all available skills stored in the skills database of the workflow execution environment.
long_term_memory.note: Persistent skills database reused across runs.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: that input workflow is marked as “incomprehensible” and the rest of the detection and consequent repairs are skipped

self_verification.evidence_quote: Timonattempts to instantiate the JSON object as a valid DSL program adhering to our specified grammar A.2 , with the support of Pydantic [ 18] type checking library
self_verification.note: Static analyzer = linters_typecheck; baseline setting where Pumbaa detects and repairs its own output without feedback = self_critique.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: we set the maximum count of repair attempts for each defect type to ten

rollback.evidence_quote: we use the initial defective workflow sample asPumbaa’s input and not the version of the workflow that has been repaired for its unreachable variable defects
rollback.note: No rollback mechanism; reuse of the original sample is an experimental control.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: iteratively prompts the FM to repair the input workflow’s defect incidences per category till all reported incidences for the target defect type are repaired or the maximum count of repair attempts is exhausted

cost_controls.evidence_quote: The cost of each repair attempt is calculated as the sum of the monetary cost corresponding to input token usage and completion token count for that specific repair attempt.
cost_controls.note: Costs are measured and a max-attempt recommendation is given, but no budget enforcement mechanism is described.

timeouts.evidence_quote: Pumbaaiteratively prompts the model to repair the sample workflow for its defect incidences per category till all reported incidences for the target defect type are repaired or the maximum count of repair attempts is exhausted
timeouts.note: Only attempt caps, no time limits; inference time is measured only.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: The general-purpose workflow execution environment that we consider in this work is capable of executingWorkflowDSLprograms by orchestratingskills
execution_isolation.note: Isolation of the execution environment is not described; Timon/Pumbaa operate statically without executing workflows.

permission_model.evidence_quote: If the target task-corresponding action does not exist within the database, that action is marked as hallucinated.
permission_model.note: Skills database acts as the allowlist of permissible actions.

tracing.evidence_quote: Timonis executed to record incidences of different defect types in that sample
tracing.note: Defect Recorder produces a structured detection report; token/cost/time metrics also recorded.

replayability.evidence_quote: Analyzed FM-generated DSL workflows, ground-truth defect annotations, analysis results, and the prompts used during experiments are made available online for replicability.
replayability.note: Artifacts released but no trajectory replay mechanism.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: To evaluate the performance ofTimon, we use the TPs, FPs, and FNs and calculate the tool’s precision and recall.
eval_hooks.note: Evaluation harness computes pass@k and precision/recall against ground truth annotations.

guardrails.evidence_quote: employing additional guardrails for ensuring the FMs’ success in synthesizing DSL program instances is inevitable
guardrails.note: Timon validates and blocks defective workflows before execution; unparsable/invalid outputs are gated and repaired.

target_domain.evidence_quote: a workflow is a sequence of smaller, atomic steps that are logically aggregated to create an automatable end-to-end process [60], wherein each step represents an invocation of an FM or a supporting software element

open_source.evidence_quote: due to data security and privacy regulations, the real-world artifacts obtained from our customers cannot be directly used for experimentation
open_source.note: Only a figshare replication package of data and prompts is released; no tool source repository is cited.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: we use and compare the repair performance of three different families of models including OpenAI’s GPT-4o-2024-08-06 ... Meta’s Llama-3-70B, and Alibaba’s Qwen-7B

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: Towards Reliable Generation of Executable Workflows by Foundation Models
primary_artifact.note: No public code repository given; coded from the paper.
